suite.fixture: A bare repository whose main branch has three commits: an SSH-signed commit adding a README, a 128 KiB binary payload, and a gitlink submodule at deps/fixture resolved through a relative URL, followed by two history commits. A lightweight tag points at the signed commit; receive and transfer fsck are enabled, and a read-only replica rejects every push.

statuses.supported: Covered by an automated stock-Git probe and part of the public contract.
statuses.local: Runs in the stock client checkout; the transport preserves the required objects and refs.
statuses.conditional: Supported when the condition in the matrix is satisfied.
statuses.unsupported: Rejected or deliberately unavailable; follow the linked recovery or alternative.

paths.label: Direct owner SSH
paths.transport: SSH (ssh://); the offline probe uses a stock smart-HTTP origin with the same pack negotiation
paths.authentication: Registered SSH public key with repository read or write permission
paths.description: A stock Git SSH session terminates at the owner-authorized forced-command gateway.

paths.label: Stable relay HTTPS
paths.transport: HTTPS smart protocol under the stable repository URL
paths.authentication: None for reading a public repository. A push to the same URL needs an account credential and goes through the authenticated push proxy, which this suite does not probe
paths.description: The stable repository URL proxies upload-pack in place from one integrity-matching HTTPS mirror.

paths.label: Relay mirror failover
paths.transport: HTTPS smart protocol through a relay-selected mirror
paths.authentication: Anonymous read of a public repository; no credentials reach a mirror
paths.description: Before response bytes are committed, the relay retries another healthy mirror with the same attested refs.

limitations.title: HTTPS pushes need a credential and are not probed by this suite
limitations.expected: A push to the stable HTTPS URL without a credential gets HTTP 401 push_unauthorized with a Basic challenge before ForkMesh reads the push body. With a credential, the relay checks that the account may write the repository and streams the push to one endpoint that accepts receive-pack; for a repository the core nodes host, that is the core that last took a push, else the first live core in rendezvous order. Read mirrors never take writes.
limitations.action: When Git asks, enter your ForkMesh account name or email and either your account password (when two-factor authentication is off) or the push credential from Settings, SSH keys, Push code over HTTPS. On the core nodes the default and protected branches only fast-forward, other branches may be force-pushed by accounts that may write them, new tags are allowed, and a push never deletes a branch.
limitations.recovery: A refused push changes no remote ref or object. Check the account name and the password or credential, then retry the same push; HTTP 403 push_forbidden means the account may not push to this repository. The Git errors page lists every message.

limitations.title: Repository-controlled server hooks are disabled
limitations.expected: Client-side hooks in a checkout run normally. Gateways set core.hooksPath to the null device so pushed repository configuration cannot execute code on a mirror.
limitations.action: Keep developer hooks local; put shared required checks in reviewed ForkMesh Actions or another CI system.
limitations.recovery: A rejected local hook leaves the index and remote unchanged; fix or intentionally bypass the local hook according to project policy.

limitations.title: A response cannot change mirrors mid-stream
limitations.expected: ForkMesh retries another eligible mirror only before response bytes are committed. An interrupted pack fails as a normal Git transport error.
limitations.action: Retry the fetch; Git reuses valid local objects and ForkMesh may select another matching mirror for the new request.
limitations.recovery: Run git fsck --full --strict if the client or disk reported corruption. Do not delete the existing clone before collecting diagnostics.

lastTested.evidence: forkmesh-stock-git v1 mirror-failover and integrity probes

limitations.title: Partial clone requires Git protocol v2
limitations.expected: A protocol-v0 filtered clone may receive the initial commits and trees, but its first lazy blob fetch is rejected as an unadvertised-object request so hidden ForkMesh objects remain inaccessible.
limitations.action: Use Git 2.34 or newer and retry with -c protocol.version=2, or omit --filter for a full clone.
limitations.recovery: Remove the incomplete disposable clone, or keep it for diagnostics and clone into a new directory with protocol v2; no remote ref or object was changed.

lastTested.evidence: forkmesh-stock-git v1 protocol-v0 rejection and protocol-v2 partial-clone probes

limitations.title: Submodules are separate repositories
limitations.expected: The superproject clone succeeds, then Git names the exact submodule whose independent URL is unavailable or unauthorized.
limitations.action: Confirm every .gitmodules URL uses a published public HTTPS route or an SSH route your key may read, then run git submodule update --init --recursive.
limitations.recovery: The superproject and any completed submodules remain valid; Git resumes the missing child without recloning successful repositories.

limitations.title: Third-party desktop UI certification is not complete
limitations.expected: GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, and GitKraken are not release-supported rows until their exact application and bundled-Git versions produce a retained report.
limitations.action: Use a tested Git CLI or ForkMesh Qt build, or run the versioned probe with the desktop application's bundled Git before relying on it.
limitations.recovery: The probe uses disposable repositories and makes no production write. Attach its JSON report when requesting a new supported row.

lastTested.evidence: No support claim is published without retained evidence.
